name: Chain Shuttling Polymerization
form_string: <Resource xmlns="http://schema.nist.gov/xml/ce-res-md/1.0wd2" xmlns:rsm="http://schema.nist.gov/xml/ce-res-md/1.0wd2" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"><identity><title>Catalytic Production of Olefin Block Copolymers via Chain Shuttling Polymerization</title></identity><providers><publisher>Science</publisher></providers><content><description>Abstract: We report a catalytic system that produces olefin block copolymers with alternating semicrystalline and amorphous segments, achieved by varying the ratio of α-olefin to ethylene in the two types of blocks. The system uses a chain shuttling agent to transfer growing chains between two distinct catalysts with different monomer selectivities in a single polymerization reactor. The block copolymers simultaneously have high melting temperatures and low glass transition temperatures, and therefore they maintain excellent elastomeric properties at high temperatures. Furthermore, the materials are effectively produced in economically favorable, continuous polymerization processes.</description><landingPage>https://www.science.org/doi/full/10.1126/science.1125268</landingPage><primaryAudience>researchers</primaryAudience></content><role xsi:type="rsm:Literature"><type>Literature: Article</type></role><applicability><productClass><durable_plastics>durable plastics</durable_plastics><packaging>packaging</packaging><packaging>packaging: plastic</packaging></productClass><lifecyclePhase><materials_design>materials design</materials_design></lifecyclePhase><materialType><polymers_chemistry-based>polymers: chemistry-based</polymers_chemistry-based><polymers_property-based>polymers: property-based</polymers_property-based></materialType></applicability></Resource>

name: Preferred Fiber & Materials Market Report
form_string:
<Resource xmlns="http://schema.nist.gov/xml/ce-res-md/1.0wd2" xmlns:rsm="http://schema.nist.gov/xml/ce-res-md/1.0wd2" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"><identity><title>Preferred Fiber & Materials Market Report</title></identity><providers><publisher>Textile Exchange</publisher></providers><content><description>2022: Key takeaways from the report
The report shows that it's unlikely for the textile industry’s
fiber and materials market to stay within 1.5°C pathway
without reducing growth, a major acceleration of transition
to preferred fiber and materials, and innovation.
The industry must: (1.) Rethink growth—the elephant in the room.
Global fiber production reached an all-time high again in
2021 after a slight decline due to COVID-19 the previous
year. Given this growth of the overall fiber and materials market and its impacts, it's increasingly important to rethink growth and decouple value creation from resource use. (2.) Speed up the shift from conventional—particularly fossil-based—to preferred fiber and materials. More than half of global growing fiber production is fossilbased. A transition to preferred sources is a must. (3.) Innovate and collaborate. Use the solutions that already exist—but also innovate and collaborate in order to accelerate progress and take the bold actions needed to scale new emerging materials and regenerative agriculture. (4.) The best way to predict the future is to create it. The forecast data shared in the report is one of multiple scenarios. While these scenarios may help the industry think about potential future pathways and impacts, the future can—and must be—influenced. We need to be part of the solution to create a planet that is habitable well into
the future. (5.) Everybody needs to be a leader. Significant acceleration in terms of climate action is needed in order to stay within the 1.5° pathway. Everybody needs to be—and can be—part of the solution.</description><landingPage>https://textileexchange.org/app/uploads/2022/10/Textile-Exchange_PFMR_2022.pdf</landingPage></content><role xsi:type="rsm:Literature"><type>Literature: Report</type></role></Resource>

form_string:

At NEU: An ACI Center of Excellence for Carbon Neutral Concrete, we realize that it is important that as new technologies come forward, they are vetted and assessed for their efficacy. To accomplish this, NEU has taken on several core functions:
- Creating a process to assess and validate the claims of innovative and new materials/technologies associated with low carbon concrete production
- Creating educational resources and programs pertaining to carbon neutral concrete production and placement.
- Representing the supply side and demand side
- Being collaborative; supporting regional and global efforts, roadmaps, etc.
- Assisting government agencies in decision making surrounding carbon neutral concrete
- Being collaborative; supporting regional and global efforts, roadmaps, etc.
- Assisting government agencies in decision making surrounding carbon neutral concrete
NEU was established by the American Concrete Institute to collaborate globally to drive education, awareness, and adoption of the use of carbon neutral materials and technologies in the built environment.  NEU has seen rapid growth since its founding and we encourage participation in our Center to help the industry meet carbon neutral goals. NEU is being established with the American Concrete Institute, a leading global authority for the development, dissemination, and adoption of its consensus-based standards, technical resources, and educational, training, and certification programs.</description><subject>carbon neutral concrete,low carbon cement and concrete</subject><landingPage>https://www.neuconcrete.org/</landingPage><primaryAudience>researchers</primaryAudience><primaryAudience>practitioners</primaryAudience></content><role xsi:type="rsm:Organization"><type>Organization: Consortium</type></role><applicability><productClass><building_materials>building materials: concrete</building_materials></productClass><lifecyclePhase><carbon_capture>carbon capture</carbon_capture><materials_design>materials design</materials_design><product_design>product design</product_design></lifecyclePhase><materialType><concrete>concrete</concrete></materialType></applicability></Resource>

name: Science paper
form_string: <Resource xmlns="http://schema.nist.gov/xml/ce-res-md/1.0wd2" xmlns:rsm="http://schema.nist.gov/xml/ce-res-md/1.0wd2" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"><identity><title>Evaluating scenarios toward zero plastic pollution</title></identity><providers><publisher>Science</publisher></providers><content><description>Article by Lau et al (2020).  Abstract:  Plastic pollution is a pervasive and growing problem. To estimate the effectiveness of interventions to reduce plastic pollution, we modeled stocks and flows of municipal solid waste and four sources of microplastics through the global plastic system for five scenarios between 2016 and 2040. Implementing all feasible interventions reduced plastic pollution by 40% from 2016 rates and 78% relative to “business as usual” in 2040. Even with immediate and concerted action, 710 million metric tons of plastic waste cumulatively entered aquatic and terrestrial ecosystems. To avoid a massive build-up of plastic in the environment, coordinated global action is urgently needed to reduce plastic consumption; increase rates of reuse, waste collection, and recycling; expand safe disposal systems; and accelerate innovation in the plastic value chain.</description><landingPage>https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.aba9475</landingPage><primaryAudience>researchers</primaryAudience><primaryAudience>educators</primaryAudience></content><role xsi:type="rsm:Literature"><type>Literature: Article</type></role></Resource>

name: Federal LCA Commons
form_string: <Resource xmlns="http://schema.nist.gov/xml/ce-res-md/1.0wd2" xmlns:rsm="http://schema.nist.gov/xml/ce-res-md/1.0wd2" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"><identity><title>Federal LCA Commons</title></identity><providers><publisher>USDA</publisher></providers><content><description>The Federal LCA Commons is an interagency community of practice for Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) research methods. This community of practice collaborates to share expertise and methods to move toward common Federal data modeling conventions and make Federal data sets freely available through a web-based data repository. The Federal LCA Commons has been formalized through a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) to establish a formal agreement to coordinate LCA data, research, and information systems between the United States Department of Agriculture, Department of Energy, and Environmental Protection Agency. Additionally, the initiative is bolstered by a number of other participating agencies across government mission areas. Participating agencies each support for their mission, programs, and stakeholders. The initiative serves to coordinate and distribute Agency mission products for public benefit. The goals of the Federal LCA Commons and its value to the public and the Federal government are to: (1) Advance Federal LCA data, research, and information systems by leveraging multi-agency resources and expertise, (2) Improve consistency in LCA methods developed by each agency to develop LCA results for decision-making and public disclosure, and (3) Enhance public and agency access to Federal LCA data in a standardized searchable format from a common repository. The Federal LCA Commons data platform uses the openLCA Collaboration Server application. The Federal LCA Commons allows users to access and download data in the JSON-LD or ILCD formats, or fetch data directly into their local openLCA desktop application.</description><subject>life cycle assessment</subject><landingPage>https://www.lcacommons.gov/</landingPage><primaryAudience>researchers</primaryAudience><primaryAudience>practitioners</primaryAudience></content><role xsi:type="rsm:Collection"><type>Collection: Repository</type></role><applicability><lifecyclePhase><end-of-life_management>end-of-life management</end-of-life_management><processing>processing</processing><use_and_reuse>use and reuse</use_and_reuse></lifecyclePhase></applicability></Resource>

name: Fostering a Circular Economy of Manufacturing Materials Workshop Report
form_string:
<Resource xmlns="http://schema.nist.gov/xml/ce-res-md/1.0wd2" xmlns:rsm="http://schema.nist.gov/xml/ce-res-md/1.0wd2" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"><identity><title>Fostering a Circular Economy of Manufacturing Materials Workshop Report</title></identity><providers><publisher>ASTM</publisher></providers><content><description>This report presents the key outcomes from the Workshop: “Fostering a Circular Economy of Manufacturing Materials” jointly organized by ASTM International and NIST, key takeaways from the proceeding Survey: Manufacturing in a Circular Economy, and next steps for addressing the standards needs identified in both.

In addition to the standards identified, two key takeaways stemmed from the survey and workshop: first, participants have a transformative, though fragmented, vision for a new way of thinking about how we create and use materials that is regenerative rather than extractive. Second, participants are motivated to make this vision come true, and they are indicative of a larger desire across the manufacturing sector to implement circularity. ASTM Committee E60 on Sustainability is well-suited to play a part in developing and coordinating standards that foster a circular economy for manufacturing materials.                            The report, and the types of standards it proposes will be of particular interest to material and product designers, manufacturing processors, recovery processors, and system planners and policymakers. These stakeholders will also be critical for realizing these CE standards. ASTM Committee E60 is initiating new efforts to address some of the standards needs and welcome other experts in the field to join and expand upon existing development activities and initiate new ones.</description><landingPage>https://marketing.astm.org/acton/fs/blocks/showLandingPage/a/9652/p/p-039d/t/page/fm/0</landingPage><primaryAudience>researchers</primaryAudience><primaryAudience>practitioners</primaryAudience><primaryAudience>policy makers</primaryAudience></content><role xsi:type="rsm:Literature"><type>Literature: Proceedings</type><type>Literature: Report</type></role><role xsi:type="rsm:Literature"><type>Literature: Proceedings</type><type>Literature: Report</type></role></Resource>

name: PV^2
form_string: <Resource xmlns="http://schema.nist.gov/xml/ce-res-md/1.0wd2" xmlns:rsm="http://schema.nist.gov/xml/ce-res-md/1.0wd2" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"><identity><title>Present Value of PhotoVoltaics</title></identity><providers><publisher>NIST</publisher></providers><content><description>Present Value of PhotoVoltaics - [PV]^2 - is a web application that allows homeowners to determine a complete cost of ownership for residential rooftop solar photovoltaic (PV) systems including purchase and operation through the system’s service life. The goal of [PV]^2 is to assist homeowners in making economical decisions related to solar PV. The current version is focused on allowing a homeowner to evaluate the cost-effectiveness of a specific solar PV system from a proposed contract from a solar installer. The homeowner will need information from the solar installer contract and their electricity bill. [PV]^2 uses the Economic Evaluation Engine (E3) API developed under the Metrics and Tools for Sustainable Buildings Project in the Net Zero Energy High Performance Building Program overseen by the Applied Economics Office (AEO) in the Engineering Laboratory (EL) at the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST). E3 provides American Society for Testing and Materials (ASTM) standards-based economic evaluation across a range of analysis types, including life cycle cost analysis (LCCA) and benefit-cost analysis (BCA).</description><subject>life cycle analysis,life cycle assessment,solar photovoltaics,life cycle cost analysis</subject><landingPage>https://pv2.nist.gov/</landingPage><primaryAudience>educators</primaryAudience><primaryAudience>policy makers</primaryAudience><primaryAudience>general public</primaryAudience></content><role xsi:type="rsm:Tool"><type>Tool: Web App</type></role><applicability><productClass><solar_panels>solar panels</solar_panels></productClass><lifecyclePhase><use_and_reuse>use and reuse</use_and_reuse></lifecyclePhase></applicability></Resource>

name: Circular Fibers Initiative
form_string: <Resource xmlns="http://schema.nist.gov/xml/ce-res-md/1.0wd2" xmlns:rsm="http://schema.nist.gov/xml/ce-res-md/1.0wd2" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" status="active" localid="https://ce-i.nist.gov/pid/rest/local/cdcs/1H8JHA1Z8Q2CNAR4"><identity><title>Circular Fibers Initiative</title></identity><providers><publisher>Circular Fibers Initiative</publisher></providers><content><description>The circular fibres initiative aims for a circular textile industry. The Circular Fibres Initiative brings together key industry stakeholders to build a circular economy for textiles, starting with clothing. Participants will work together to define a vision for a new global textiles system, which addresses the significant drawbacks of the current system of fast fashion. The new system for textiles is based on the principles of a circular economy, generating growth that benefits citizens and businesses, while phasing out negative impacts such as waste and pollution. The Circular Fibres Initiative already involves more than 20 leading businesses, NGOs, philanthropic organisations, and public bodies. As a first step, the Circular Fibres Initiative produced an analysis of the textiles industry, mapping how textiles flow around the global economy, and the externalities that arise from the current system. It explores what a new, circular economy for textiles - one that is restorative and regenerative - could look like, and lay out the steps needed to build it. he initiative’s first report was published in November 2017, and together with the accompanying stakeholder consultation informs the initiative’s further activities. They help put together textile economy reports which can be found on their website.</description><subject>fibres,fashion ,textile industry</subject><landingPage>https://www.stateoffashion.org/en/learn/circular-fibres-initiative-aims-circular-textile-industry/</landingPage><primaryAudience>researchers</primaryAudience><primaryAudience>general public</primaryAudience></content><role xsi:type="rsm:Organization"><type>Organization: General/Other</type></role><applicability><productClass><textiles>textiles</textiles></productClass></applicability></Resource>
